lifecycle: CordisBoundNodeHost.executeNode -> verify real Cordis fibers ACTIVE -> plan hash match -> NodeContainer.execute_with_plan_hash -> typed NodeExecutionOutput
CordisBoundNodeHost.drain -> NodeContainer.drain when measured in_flight is zero
CordisBoundNodeHost.dispose -> verify Rust state is draining or failed -> reverse Cordis Fiber disposal -> NodeContainer.dispose
mount failure -> NodeContainer.fail -> reverse Cordis Fiber disposal -> NodeContainer.dispose
graph_binding_rule: the actual mounted Cordis plugin plan entries must equal the immutable NodePluginPlan entries; graph_hash, manifest_hash, loaded_plan_hash and plan.hash must be the same verified hash before Rust declaration
in_flight_rule: Rust NodeContainer exclusively owns the atomic in-flight count; the JS host consumes typed status without storing a second counter; drain rejects when the Rust count is non-zero
transport_rule: the host port is a persistent line-delimited typed operation channel; the JS encoder exposes only declared lifecycle/execute methods and the Rust decoder rejects every field outside that operation's schema; lifecycle messages carry only lifecycle status or v4.node_container.lifecycle_failure facts; execute messages carry only typed data/control input, plan hash, typed data/control/diagnostics output or v4.node_container.execution_failure facts; never carry business payload, protocol metadata, MetadataCenter state or product Error01-06 state
execution_rule: real Cordis plugin fibers must be mounted and ACTIVE and their planEntry list must equal the immutable NodePluginPlan entries before execute; execute sends only the active plan hash plus typed NodeExecutionInput; Rust NodeContainer.execute_with_plan_hash rejects plan hash drift, invalid state and unregistered/effect-violating handles; NodeExecutionOutput keeps data, control and diagnostics as separate typed fields
execution_response_rule: JS port #settle dispatches the response schema by pending op: lifecycle success must NOT project output; execute_node success carries only {ok, request_id, state, in_flight, output} where output is the typed NodeExecutionOutput; execute_node failure is a v4.node_container.execution_failure fact; the two decoders never accept the other's fields
failure_rule: NodeContainer lifecycle failures are recorded by the lifecycle-dispatch owner as typed v4.node_container.lifecycle_failure facts and projected on the same lifecycle port; they do not enter v4.control.error_chain because this management channel has no product request/session/target scope and must not fabricate one
execution_failure_rule: NodeContainer execution failures are recorded by the execution-dispatch owner as typed v4.node_container.execution_failure facts and projected on the same host port; they do not enter v4.control.error_chain because this management channel has no product request/session/target scope and must not fabricate one
forbidden: generic operation plus arbitrary fields encoder
unknown lifecycle request fields silently discarded
execution input/output fields merged into a single control/data blob
control/debug/error fields in provider or client business payload
required_tests: real Cordis mount drives Rust state to accepting
in-flight execution rejects drain and leaves state accepting
accepting-state disposal rejects before either lifecycle owner is mutated
Cordis graph/plan drift rejects before Rust declaration
Cordis mount failure drives Rust candidate through failed to disposed
real Cordis fibers drive ordered Rust NodePluginPlan execution
execution plan hash mismatch fails before Rust handles run
unregistered plugin handle fails fast with typed execution failure
JS and Rust reject undeclared execution fields
JS execution response decoder rejects malformed output
Rust rejects metadata and business fields outside the selected lifecycle operation schema
JS rejects undeclared lifecycle fields before writing to the port
lifecycle failure projection retains resource id, request id, node id, operation, typed code and message
